monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp increase in intensity and efficiency despite drastically fewer runs, indicating a strategic shift toward higher-quality sessions.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite only one run this month so far, the runner achieved their best pace of the period (531 sec/km) with elevated aerobic training effect (3.5) — suggesting strong acute readiness and effective pacing execution.

goal_tracker.message: You need 36.0 more km across 9 additional sessions to match last month's volume — averaging 4.0 km per session over the remaining 27 days.

insights.title: Efficiency dip correlates with higher-intensity distribution
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.42 to 12.81 this month, coinciding with a major shift in HR zone distribution: Zone 3–5 time rose from 22% to 55% (19% → 26% Z3, 3% → 22% Z4, 0% → 7% Z5), indicating less time spent in highly efficient fat-oxidation zones.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance signals increased threshold work
insights.body: Zone 4 contribution jumped from 3% (last month) to 22% (this month), while Zone 1+2 dropped from 79% to 46% — reflecting a deliberate, but potentially unsustainable, emphasis on lactate threshold efforts without proportional recovery or base-building support.

insights.title: Cadence improved while vertical oscillation increased slightly
insights.body: Cadence rose from 146 to 154 spm, yet vertical oscillation increased from 7.5–7.8 cm (last month’s recent runs) to 7.9 cm (June 1), suggesting faster turnover may be accompanied by marginally less economical bounce — possibly due to fatigue or intensity-driven form compromise.

insights.title: VO2 max remains stable despite shifting load
insights.body: VO2 max is unchanged at 37.0 across all five recent runs, confirming physiological consistency — however, the jump in aerobic TE (from 2.4–3.0 to 3.5) and HR (132→147 bpm) on June 1 indicates that the same VO2 max is now being taxed more acutely, signaling rising internal load.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run at ≤135 bpm within the next 48 hours, focusing on relaxed breathing and cadence ≥152 spm.
recommendations.reason: To restore Zone 1–2 volume (now at just 46% this month vs 79% last month) and rebuild aerobic efficiency, which dropped to 12.81 — a level associated with reduced fat-oxidation capacity.

recommendations.action: Repeat the 2.1 km 'fast finish' effort from May 30 (8:23 min/km, 142 bpm, 143 spm) as a standalone 2.5 km Zone 3 cruise at 140–145 bpm, emphasizing stride length ≥80 cm.
recommendations.reason: That session showed the highest stride length (81.96 cm) and lowest ground contact (320 ms) in the dataset — indicating neuromuscular freshness worth reinforcing before fatigue accumulates.

recommendations.action: Add a 10-minute post-run mobility routine targeting hip flexors and calves after your next two runs, given vertical oscillation increased to 7.9 cm and ground contact time remained >310 ms across all recent runs — signs of reduced elastic recoil.
recommendations.reason: Elevated vertical oscillation (+0.4 cm vs May avg) and sustained ground contact (>310 ms) suggest stiffness or fatigue limiting spring-like efficiency.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational endurance by prioritizing time-in-zone over pace, restoring fat-oxidation capacity, and protecting running economy through lower-intensity volume and targeted mobility.
suggested_sessions: 4 km conversational pace with cadence focus (≥152 spm)
